cards.title: and, or, not
cards.body: `and` is True only when both sides are True. `or` is True when at least one side is. `not` flips True and False.
cards.code:
print(True and False)
print(True or False)
print(not True)

cards.title: Combining conditions
cards.body: Join comparisons to describe a whole rule in one condition.

cards.title: Brackets make it clear
cards.body: Python works out `and` before `or`. Brackets make the order obvious, to you and to Python.

cards.title: Spot the bug
cards.body: It calls everyone a teenager, even a 40-year-old. Which line is wrong?

bug.fix: With `or`, one true side is enough, and every age is `>= 13` or `<= 19`. Both must be true, so use `and`.

check.question: What does this print?
check.explanation: 1900 divides by 4, but it also divides by 100, so y % 100 != 0 is False, and and needs both sides True.

exercise.prompt: Read a year and print `leap` if it is a leap year, otherwise `common`. A year is a leap year if it divides by 4, except that years dividing by 100 are not, unless they also divide by 400.
